title: TravelTech meetup talk
text:
I spoke at Edinburgh’s TravelTech meetup last night. It’s a friendly event organised by Joshua Ryan-Saha and Maddy Burgoyne.
My talk was on using OpenStreetMap data, and despite the session topic I used no AI. I think it was appropriate as I included tips on accessing OSM data in a sustainable way and structured data is very much AI ready.
You can view my slides on Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.24531364
I spoke about some of the ways I’ve used OSM data in the past, along with a challenge to the community about Le Tour De France preparedness! Joshua asked a great question on what am I currently working on.





I took a sabbatical in the summer and cycled to Denmark with my family. It was a great opporunity to compare communities between home and the three countries we cycled through. Unsurpringly, I had lots of thoughts about accommodation and resilience! Here’s my notebook page, hopefully I’ll get to look at some of these in 2027:

title: Software and tools
text:
This is a non-exhaustive list of the software and data types I work with. For examples please see my blog or get in touch to discuss your support requirements.


 email Mike



Programming

R: Statistical and programming software
RStudio: Development environment for R
Quarto, LaTeX and Markdown: Document automation
Linux, Bash and associated tools: for scaling and automation
Git: Version control software (for use with Github, Bitbucket, Gitlab, Codeberg, etc.)
Kate IDE a lightweight development environment

Spatial and GIS

GRASS: Geographic information system
QGIS: Geographic information system

Data storage

SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL
Parquet, Arrow and partitioned data

Other

Scribus: Desktop publishing
Logseq: personal knowledge management - easy notetaking and information retrieval
KeePassXC: password management


My operating system of choice is Fedora, which is built on Linux. A lot of the software on this page is also available for Windows and Macs. I switched from using Windows to Linux in early 2011 and have not regretted the decision.
I’ve a help wiki of resources I find useful. Hopefully you find them useful too!
Some of the software listed above have great communities, here are those I work with:

EdinbR a meetup for users of R
OSGeo:UK is an umbrella organisation for spatial software
PyData Edinburgh a meetup for users of Python

title: About Mike
text:
Mike is a data professional supporting organisations with leadership, research, scaling, automation and more. His background is in climate science, and has since worked in a range of fields including economics, sociology, agriculture, mental health, finance and social care. Across these domains Mike has used data skills like programming, GIS, data management, modelling, and visualisation to solve challenges and help organisations find solutions.
Mike has a PhD from the University of Edinburgh, where he studied snow hydrology. His research was based around a historic dataset (Snow Survey of Great Britain), which he used to demonstrate a link between snow cover and climate fluctuations and better understand snow cover and melt frequency through computer simulation, machine learning and statistics. You can read more about Mike’s research on his (retired) academic blog, scottishsnow.
Prior to his PhD Mike worked as a hydrologist for Environment Agency Wales and Halcrow Group Ltd. He worked on projects including river and coastal flood mapping, flood defence scheme design, river re-alignment, flood forecasting (operationally and model development) and flood risk assessment. Mike graduated from Lancaster University in 2004 with a BSc (hons) in Environmental Science.
Mike is a fellow of the Royal Statistical Society and member of the Society of Research Software Engineers.
